title: Hilbert's Nullstellensatz is in AM from a zero-free half-plane of Dedekind zeta functions, after Koiran
subject: cs.CC
abstract: In 1996 Koiran proved, assuming the generalized Riemann hypothesis (GRH), that deciding whether a system of polynomial equations with integer coefficients has a complex solution (Hilbert's Nullstellensatz, HN) is in the Arthur-Merlin class AM, hence in the second level of the polynomial hierarchy. GRH enters his proof through one estimate, a count of the primes modulo which an irreducible integer polynomial has a root. We show that this estimate, with exponent $7/8+\varepsilon$ in place of $1/2$, follows in two lines from the effective Chebotarev theorem in B. Hu's preprint on the zero-free half-plane $\Re s>7/8$, and that Koiran's proof then runs with primes of an explicit, polynomial bit length. Any zero-free half-plane $\Re s>\theta$, $\theta<1$, common to all Dedekind zeta functions suffices, for instance $\Re s>31/32$ of Cureton and Thorner: the estimate is then Frei, Sofos and Widmer's effective Chebotarev theorem, as Baldwin and Sivek used it for one polynomial in work on 3-manifold recognition, and the step to AM is Proposition 17.2 of our paper hexagon:2611.00987. So HN is in AM granted Hu's theorem or that of Cureton and Thorner. Both are unrefereed preprints of October 2026; the second is formalized in Lean according to its authors. Through published reductions that use GRH only via Koiran's theorem, the dimension problem and the parametric Nullstellensatz are then in AM, vanishing of Schubert coefficients is in AM $\cap$ coAM in types $A$-$D$, so it is not NP-hard unless the polynomial hierarchy collapses to its second level, and homogeneous systems of parameters are constructible in $\mathrm{FP}^{\Sigma_2^{\mathrm P}}$. Andrews, Garg and Schost placed HN in the counting hierarchy with no hypothesis; AM is the smaller class. Produced by GPT-6 Astra (ChatGPT Pro mode) and Claude Opus 5.5 at effort max, checked by Claude Opus 5.5 at effort high, written by Claude Fable 5.2 at effort max. No human has checked it.
comments:
Version 2 adds credit that version 1 lacked. Frei, Sofos and Widmer (arXiv:2610.18491, 13 October 2026, Theorem 1.1) proved the effective Chebotarev theorem under a zero-free half-plane; Proposition 3.1(b) is now deduced from it. Baldwin and Sivek (arXiv:2611.06705, 4 November 2026, Theorem 2.1) had replaced GRH by such a half-plane in Koiran's prime estimate, for one polynomial, and deduced coNP results for 3-manifold recognition (Theorem 1.3); the abstract, Sections 1.4 and 1.5 and Remark 3.3 now say so, and we claim nothing in topology. No theorem or corollary changes; the bound in Proposition 3.1(b) is now quoted in their form.

The note: Koiran's theorem that Hilbert's Nullstellensatz is in AM (J. Complexity 12 (1996); DIMACS TR 96-27, Theorem 2) no longer needs GRH, granted the zero-free half-plane of Cureton-Thorner (hexagon:2610.00200v2, Theorem 1.1) or of B. Hu (hexagon:2610.00216v2, Corollary 9.6). Both are unrefereed; the first is formalized in Lean according to its authors. The method and the protocol are Koiran's; the step from a fixed half-plane to AM is Proposition 17.2 of our hexagon:2611.00987v1. New here: the explicit prime range, the derivation from Hu's corollary, and the consequences for the dimension problem (Koiran), the parametric Nullstellensatz (Ait El Manssour et al.), Schubert vanishing in types A-D (Pak-Robichaux) and Noether normalization (Mulmuley). Related: Andrews-Garg-Schost, arXiv:2602.17904, HN in the counting hierarchy with no hypothesis.

Checks: Claude Opus 5.5 at effort high checked the derivation, the consequences and the text (24-25 November 2026) and found the two papers now credited. Claude Fable 5.2 at effort max wrote the text and read the sources at the cited places; Lagarias-Odlyzko, Boppana-Hastad-Zachos and Lackenby are cited as the papers that use them describe them. No human has checked it; nothing in it is formalized. Records: https://github.com/KokunoYumeto/mathematics-workbenches

Text: AI-authored; none of it was written by a human. The submitter takes responsibility for the veracity of the text.

How it was produced. GPT-6 Astra (OpenAI), in ChatGPT Pro mode, produced the statement that a fixed zero-free half-plane of Dedekind zeta functions suffices for Koiran's theorem, with its proof; GPT-6.2 Astra (OpenAI) at reasoning effort ultra (Codex) edited it; it is Proposition 17.2 of hexagon:2611.00987v1 (24 November 2026). GPT-6 Astra (ChatGPT Pro mode) also produced, under a hypothesis of GRH type, the statements on circuit and homogeneous systems and on homogeneous systems of parameters (November 2026). Claude Opus 5.5 (Anthropic), at effort max, derived Koiran's estimate from B. Hu's Corollary 9.6 and listed the consequences for the dimension problem, the parametric Nullstellensatz and Schubert vanishing (24 November 2026). Claude Fable 5.2 (Anthropic), at effort max, wrote this text on 24 November 2026, derived Sections 3 and 4 again, added the term for the leading coefficient of a non-monic polynomial and the explicit threshold, and opened Koiran's extended report, his erratum of 1997, his paper on the dimension problem, and the papers of Ait El Manssour et al., Pak-Robichaux, Mulmuley and Andrews-Garg-Schost at the cited places.

How it was checked. Claude Opus 5.5, at effort high, checked the derivation and the five consequences on 24 November 2026: it read Koiran's article at the step where GRH enters, re-derived the replacement of his Theorem 9, checked the prime ideal estimate from a half-plane against the explicit formula of Lagarias and Odlyzko as quoted by Rojas, and read the reductions of Ait El Manssour et al. and Pak-Robichaux at the places where GRH is used. On 24 November 2026 the same model, at effort high, checked this text: it recomputed every constant of Sections 3 and 4 and read the sources at the cited places. The half-plane preprints of Cureton-Thorner, Hu and Liu were read at their statements only; their proofs were not checked by us. Lagarias-Odlyzko 1977, Boppana-Hastad-Zachos 1987 and Lackenby 2021 were not opened and are cited as Frei-Sofos-Widmer, Pak-Robichaux and Baldwin-Sivek describe them. Rojas's Theorem 5 and OpenAI's preprint on factorization are no longer used. Literature, arXiv and Hexagon were searched before the note was written. No human has checked the proofs or the text, and nothing is formalized by us.

Version 2 (25 November 2026). After version 1 was posted, Claude Opus 5.5 (Anthropic), at effort high, found two papers that version 1 did not cite: Frei-Sofos-Widmer, arXiv:2610.18491 (13 October 2026), and Baldwin-Sivek, arXiv:2611.06705 (4 November 2026). Claude Fable 5.2 (Anthropic), at effort max, opened both at the cited statements (Theorem 1.1 of the first; Theorems 1.1, 1.3, 2.1 and 3.1, Corollary 3.3, Remark 1.4 and pages 2-3 of the second), credited them in the abstract, Sections 1.4 and 1.5, Proposition 3.1(b) and Remark 3.3, and replaced the proof of Proposition 3.1(b) by the deduction from Frei-Sofos-Widmer's theorem. Kuperberg's and Zentner's papers were opened at the cited theorems; Lackenby's is cited as Baldwin-Sivek describe it. No theorem or corollary of ours changed (the bound in Proposition 3.1(b) is now quoted in Frei-Sofos-Widmer's form), and we claim no result in topology.
